summary.text: 几 is traditionally interpreted as a picture of a small stool or table. In simplified Chinese, the same written form also spells quantity words written 幾 in traditional Chinese; this is a separate word, not a meaning shown to have developed from the furniture term.

formation.text: The character is analyzed as a whole pictograph of a small stool or table. This traditional interpretation is not independently confirmed by an inspected early glyph image.

components.text: The whole graph 几 is interpreted as a picture of a small stool or table. It is not divided into modern lookalikes, and no separate phonetic element is supported.

history.text: A traditional account calls 几 a pictograph and associates it with ritual furniture. Later commentary describes a raised flat top with a support below; this is an interpretation of the strokes, not a verified observation of an early form.

The form 𠀃 is recorded as a variant associated with 几, with a note that it was used for both 且 and 几. The evidence does not establish it as an ancestor or support the claim that its bottom stroke represents the ground.

uncertainties.text: The traditional pictographic account is not independently confirmed by an inspected early glyph image, and the character’s earliest date has not been established by the evidence presented here.
The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison does not establish the pictured object’s original spoken name or show that 几 was borrowed to write another word.

senses.text: The earliest meaning supported here is a furniture term, traditionally glossed as a small stool or table. The precise object and the graph’s earliest date remain unresolved.

senses.gloss: how many; how much; a few
senses.text: In simplified Chinese, 几 also writes quantity words represented by 幾 in traditional Chinese. This is a spelling convention for a distinct word, not a demonstrated development from the furniture meaning.

limitations.text: No dated sequence links the furniture sense to the quantity spelling, so no semantic development between them is claimed.
The original spoken name of the pictured object has not been established; the proposed word comparison does not demonstrate borrowing.

components.text: Read 几 as one whole picture, traditionally identified as a small stool or table; no inspected early image independently confirms that interpretation.

takeaway.text: The quantity spelling 几 represents a different word from the furniture character; traditional Chinese writes that quantity word as 幾.
